description: Verify that DUT does NOT reassemble fragments whose Identification fields differ — the (src, dst, protocol, id) tuple is the reassembly bucket key (RFC 791 §3.2)
approach:
[Objective]
Fragments with different Identification numbers belong to different datagrams and must never be merged. This case sends fragment 0 with id=A and fragment 1 with id=B (otherwise compatible) and confirms DUT does not glue them together.

[Scenario — chronological]
1. Tester → DUT: fragment 0 with id=A (MF=1)
2. Tester → DUT: fragment 1 with id=B (MF=0, otherwise compatible)
   ⇒ Two separate buckets — neither should reassemble alone (each is missing the other half).

3. Observation (3 s window):
   • DUT → Tester: no Echo Reply (no completed reassembly)

[Pass condition]
DUT does not emit any Echo Reply within the window.

[Fail condition]
• Fail_early_reply — DUT replied — it merged fragments with different ids (RFC 791 §3.2 violation)
• Fail_echo_id / Fail_echo_seq / Fail_data_mismatch — Reply emitted but with wrong fields (also failure mode of merging)
• Fail_timeout — neutral catch-all if no reply observed (this is also Pass shape)

verdicts.Pass: DUT did not merge differently-identified fragments — normal
verdicts.Fail_early_reply: DUT emitted a Reply — it incorrectly merged across different IDs
verdicts.Fail_echo_id: Reply emitted with wrong identifier — bucket-key violation
verdicts.Fail_echo_seq: Reply emitted with wrong sequence — bucket-key violation
verdicts.Fail_data_mismatch: Reply emitted but data did not match expected — bucket-key violation
verdicts.Fail_timeout: No reply observed — typically the Pass shape
